name: l04-regex-map
title: Regex metacharacters
spec: Grid of labelled cells, monospace pattern then meaning: . any single character; * zero or more of the preceding item; + one or more (extended); ? zero or one (extended); ^ start of line; $ end of line; [abc] one of the set; [^abc] not in the set; {n,m} n to m repetitions; \. a literal dot. Orange note: . matches exactly one arbitrary character, and .* is greedy.
alt: A grid of common regular expression metacharacters and what each matches.
cap: Most characters match themselves, and a small set of metacharacters carries special meaning.

name: l04-bre-ere
title: BRE versus ERE
spec: Two columns. Left, BRE (default in grep and sed): + ? | () { } are literal text unless preceded by a backslash. Right, ERE (grep -E, sed -E, awk): the same characters are operators straight away, a literal plus needs a backslash. Bottom row of tools: GNU grep -P enables Perl-compatible expressions, not on macOS grep. Green bar: use -E unless you have a reason not to.
alt: Basic and extended regular expressions treat plus, question mark, pipe, parentheses and braces oppositely.
cap: BRE treats those characters as literal unless escaped, while ERE treats them as operators.

name: l04-sed-substitute
title: Anatomy of sed substitute
spec: Large monospace line: sed 's/old/new/g' file. Labels: s substitute command, old pattern, new replacement, g all matches on each line (without g only the first), file input. Below three small rows: sed -E 's/step=([0-9]+)/STEP:\1/' file with note \1 is the first capture group; sed 's|/usr/local|/opt|g' file other delimiter; sed -n '10,20p' file prints lines 10 to 20. Orange note: sed writes to standard output, -i edits the file in place.
alt: The parts of a sed substitute command with a few variations.
cap: sed applies an edit to each line as it passes through and does not change the file unless asked.
